summary.statement: Procore is the most-used project management software (46.2% in 2021) and markets AI agents that draft daily logs from photos and summarize progress for stakeholders.
Point tools cover parts of the workflow: CompanyCam (photos plus AI-generated reports), Raken (mobile daily reports) and OpenSpace (360° progress capture).
Many firms still rely on spreadsheets, free templates, and email or text.
Lenders separately pay third-party monitoring firms for monthly progress reports.
Verifiable complaints about Procore's daily log come only from competitors (click-heavy for field staff; complex suites aren't user friendly).
No independent user reviews of Procore's AI agents could be verified; review sites block Preuve's crawler. This needs interviews with Procore users.

competitors.name: Procore
competitors.description: Market-leading construction management platform. Its built-in AI agents draft daily logs from field photos, notes and audio, and turn logs into stakeholder progress summaries.

sentiment.statement: A competitor claims its daily log workflows are click-heavy and hard to navigate for field staff (biased source).

competitors.name: CompanyCam
competitors.description: Jobsite photo documentation app that markets AI-generated reports, captions and updates from site capture.

competitors.name: Raken
competitors.description: Mobile daily-reporting app for field teams, with voice-to-text entry, automatic weather capture and photo attachments.
competitors.pricing_note: Published (undated article): $12, $30 or $37 per user per month, billed annually.

competitors.name: Constructable
competitors.description: Daily logs plus project management at a flat fee with unlimited users, positioned as a simpler alternative to Procore.
competitors.pricing_note: Flat fee with unlimited users (amount not published on the cited page).

competitors.name: OpenSpace
competitors.description: 360° camera walkthroughs stitched by AI into a navigable visual record of site progress. It covers progress capture, not written reports.

competitors.name: Spreadsheets and free report templates
competitors.description: Excel or Sheets and free weekly progress report templates, filled in by hand.

competitors.name: Email, text and phone
competitors.description: Project data and updates shared ad hoc by email, text and calls rather than dedicated apps.

competitors.name: Lender construction monitoring firms (e.g. Partner Engineering and Science, RLB)
competitors.description: Third-party firms hired by lenders to visit the site, typically monthly, and write independent progress reports. They serve the lender, not the contractor.

current_solutions.statement: Reporting is done inside the dominant platform, Procore, which now ships AI agents for daily logs and stakeholder progress summaries.
Specialized apps cover parts of the workflow: photo documentation with AI reports (CompanyCam), daily reports (Raken, Constructable) and visual progress capture (OpenSpace).
Many firms still fall back on spreadsheets, free templates, and email or text.
For lenders, monthly progress reporting is often outsourced to third-party monitoring firms.
The space is crowded at the data-capture and daily-log level; any opening is more likely in owner- or lender-specific report assembly.
